text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: db-progress.md
@@
 - [ ] Runner isolation. Run `agent:run` without signing in. Verify it uses defaults and writes nothing to user tables.
 - [ ] Failure states. Verify readable errors or safe fallbacks for database downtime, expired sessions, invalid settings, and failed turn writes. Log failed writes and keep chat working.
+
+## Study and plan
+
+Baseline is `betterlook` at `8ceb7805`. The agent exposes the original `TurnRecord`, `TurnEvent`, and `AgentMessage` types, and `runAgent()` returns both the UI stream and a turn promise. Agent limits and tool policy are static. No Settings schema or localStorage-backed Settings panel is present on this ref. The workspace stores chat and sandbox ID in localStorage. Sources: `apps/web/src/lib/agent/types.ts`, `config.ts`, `run.ts`, `policy.ts`, and `apps/web/src/workspace/Workspace.tsx`.
+
+### Onlook v1
+
+- Keep the Supabase-managed `auth.users` reference, the matching public profile with cascading delete, and the project → conversation → message hierarchy with typed JSONB message parts. Use Supabase SSR cookies and Next's session-refresh proxy, with `auth.getUser()` in server handlers. Use server-only Drizzle over postgres-js with `prepare: false` and a development-cached connection. Use the Supabase CLI local stack and drizzle-kit with Supabase roles, public-schema migrations under `supabase/migrations`, and RLS on every product table. Sources: `upstream/v1:packages/db/src/schema/`, `packages/db/src/client.ts`, `packages/db/drizzle.config.ts`, `apps/web/client/src/proxy.ts`, `apps/web/client/src/utils/supabase/`, and `apps/web/client/src/server/api/trpc.ts`.
+- Drop the role join table for the single-owner MVP, pending founder confirmation. Keep the existing Next route handlers. Omit upstream tRPC, browser data and storage access, branches, canvas, frames, domains, subscriptions, invitations, and extra project and message fields. Sources: `upstream/v1:packages/db/src/schema/user/user-project.ts`, `project/project.ts`, `chat/conversation.ts`, `chat/message.ts`, and `apps/web/client/src/utils/supabase/client/index.ts`.
+- Onlook's Drizzle connection bypassed RLS. A signed-in user was sufficient for routes that skipped membership checks, exposing other users' resources. The fix applied resolve-then-verify checks, scoped provider sandbox listings and pinned self-service writes to the session. Its sandbox guard still allowed IDs without a project for bootstrap. Betterlook provisions a sandbox server-side for an owned project and records the association before accepting reconnect or restore requests. A supplied sandbox ID without an owned project gets the shared resource error. Source: `git show 423e2e92`.
+
+### Proposed schema and routes
+
+`id` is the primary key unless stated otherwise. All timestamps use `timestamptz`. Foreign keys follow the ownership chain and cascade on deletion. `auth.users` is a reference managed by Supabase. Route names marked new are proposed.
+
+| Table | Columns | Route reads and writes |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `users` | `id uuid` (PK and FK to `auth.users.id`), `created_at` | The Supabase sign-in callback verifies the user and inserts the profile idempotently. |
+| `user_settings` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema | `user_id uuid` (PK and FK to `users`), `settings jsonb` | New `GET /api/settings` reads the session user's row. New `PUT /api/settings` validates, clamps, and upserts it. `POST /api/chat` reads it for effective agent settings and trace consent. |
+| `projects` | `id uuid`, `owner_id uuid` (FK to `users`), `name text`, `sandbox_id text` (unique and nullable during provisioning), `created_at`, `updated_at` | `POST /api/chat` creates the project on first send and records the provisioned sandbox. New `GET /api/projects` lists the caller's projects and their conversations. `POST /api/sandbox` reconnects the project's sandbox. `POST /api/restore` uses the sandbox resolved from the turn. |
+| `conversations` | `id uuid`, `project_id uuid` (FK to `projects`), `created_at`, `updated_at` | `POST /api/chat` creates the first conversation and updates its timestamp on new activity. `GET /api/projects` lists owned conversations. New `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads the owned conversation, history, and usage totals. |
+| `messages` | `id bigint` (server-assigned identity, serialized as a string for `UIMessage.id`), `conversation_id uuid` (FK to `conversations`), `role`, `parts jsonb`, `metadata jsonb`, `usage jsonb` (nullable), `created_at`. `parts`, `metadata`, and `usage` are pending turn record v2 / settings schema. | `POST /api/chat` loads stored history, appends validated user input and the server-produced assistant message, and resolves approval responses to stored requests. `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads messages in append order. |
+| `turns` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema | `id uuid` (agent turn ID), `message_id bigint` (FK to the assistant `messages` row), `trace_id text`, `checkpoint_id text` (nullable), `status text`, `stop_reason text` (nullable), `provider text`, `model text`, `config_hash text`, `input_tokens bigint`, `output_tokens bigint`, `cache_read_tokens bigint`, `cache_write_tokens bigint`, `cost_usd numeric` (nullable), `created_at` | `POST /api/chat` writes a product summary when the agent turn settles. `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads turn data for history and aggregates that conversation's totals for Context & cost. `POST /api/restore` and `POST /api/events` resolve the owned turn. |
+| `events` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema | `id bigint` (identity), `turn_id uuid` (FK to `turns`), `type` (`restore`, `keep`, `approve`, `deny`), `reason text`, `tool_call_id text` (nullable), `created_at` | `POST /api/restore` records a successful restore. `POST /api/events` appends keep. `POST /api/chat` records approve or deny against the turn that requested approval. `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads action state for restored history. |
+
+### Contract differences and pending mappings
+
+- **`user_settings.settings` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** The shared server schema supplies the JSONB type, clamps and defaults for models and effort per route, thinking display, step cap, per-turn budget and cost cap, tool toggles, protected paths, approval mode, context editing and compaction, and trace consent. Parse and clamp on both reads and writes, with safe defaults for missing or invalid rows. Use the resolved settings for each turn so a saved change is reflected in the next effective config hash. Source: current `lib/agent/config.ts` and `lib/agent/run.ts` under `apps/web/src`.
+- **`messages.parts`, `messages.metadata`, `messages.usage` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** Persist server-produced AI SDK parts, including unchanged thinking and reasoning, with no client-supplied assistant history. The proposed extra `metadata` column carries the selected model and server-generated UI notice, which the current renderer uses. Rehydrate turn ID, trace ID and status from the linked turn. Append approval events and continuations and preserve the original message rows. Sources: `lib/agent/types.ts`, `lib/agent/client.ts`, `lib/agent/run.ts`, and `components/ai/Message.tsx` under `apps/web/src`.
+- **`turns` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** Confirm turn and message linkage, trace and checkpoint IDs, status and stop reason, provider and model, effective config hash, each token counter, cost, and the creation timestamp. The baseline has separate system prompt and tool config hashes, `stepLimitReached` and optional error text, nested nullable `checkpoint.id`, and `startedAt` and `endedAt`. Usage has input, output and `cachedInputTokens`, plus nullable `costUsd` initialized to `null`. It collects cache reads and exposes no cache-write total or explicit stop reason. Use the final record for these mappings. Sources: `lib/agent/types.ts` and `lib/agent/run.ts` under `apps/web/src`.
+- **`events` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** Confirm the turn link, event types, reason, tool-call correlation and timestamp. The baseline has `at`, optional `traceId`, a `checkpointId` for restore, and `toolCallId` for approve and deny. There is no event `reason`, and approvals are currently logged at continuation. The proposed `tool_call_id` preserves which request was answered when a turn has multiple tool calls. Resolve trace and checkpoint IDs from the owned turn. Sources: `lib/agent/types.ts`, `lib/agent/events.ts`, and `lib/agent/run.ts` under `apps/web/src`.
+
+### Access and persistence
+
+- `requireUser` verifies the Supabase user for data routes. `requireProject` scopes by `projects.owner_id`. `requireConversation`, `requireMessage`, `requireTurn`, and `requireEvent` follow the stored parent chain to that project. `requireSandbox` maps the sandbox ID to that same owned project. `requireSettings` scopes by the authenticated user ID. Project lists and settings writes derive the owner from the session. Signed-in requests for missing or foreign resources get the same `404` and `Unauthorized or not found` body. A request with multiple IDs must resolve them to the same resource chain before any tool, provider, checkpoint, trace or write operation. Enable RLS on each product table as defense in depth and keep the browser on Supabase Auth only.
+- `/api/chat` currently takes browser-supplied history and sandbox ID. Use the owned conversation's saved history and project sandbox, validate the submitted user input or approval, and verify an approval against its stored pending tool call. `/api/restore` derives checkpoint, sandbox and trace IDs from the owned turn. `/api/events` derives the trace ID the same way. Reconnect failures surface as errors so an existing conversation keeps its sandbox association. `/workspace/preview` is a static placeholder. The existing ChatGPT model-credential endpoints carry no product database state. Sources: `app/api/chat/route.ts`, `app/api/restore/route.ts`, `app/api/events/route.ts`, `app/api/sandbox/route.ts`, and `app/workspace/preview/route.ts` under `apps/web/src`.
+- Store product state and the trace ID in Postgres. Keep provider credentials on their current path. `runAgent()` uses the server-resolved consent value. Consent on sends the redacted full turn record to Langfuse. Consent off exports only trace ID, model, config hash, status, tokens and timing, including for nested spans and events. The CLI calls the agent with defaults and no database writes or session dependency. Replace workspace localStorage with server reads and writes, with no import. Log turn-write failures with a safe diagnostic and allow the chat stream to complete. Sources: `lib/agent/run.ts`, `lib/agent/trace.ts`, `lib/agent/events.ts`, and `workspace/Workspace.tsx` under `apps/web/src`, and `apps/web/scripts/agent-run.ts`.
+
+### Founder decisions
+
+1. Which sign-in methods should ship? Default is GitHub OAuth plus email magic link.
+2. Should projects use `projects.owner_id` or a membership join table? The proposed schema uses `owner_id` for single-owner projects.
+3. Should Supabase stay local for now or should we target Supabase Cloud as well?
+
+The study item stays open until AI-CORE-2 supplies turn record v2 and the Settings schema and the founder answers these questions. Local stack, Drizzle, and migrations wait for the orchestrator's go-ahead.
*** End Patch"));

3:- [ ] Study and plan. Read the Betterlook turn record and settings schema, then the specified Onlook v1 files and authorization commit. Record what to keep and drop, the ownership model and access helpers, tables and columns, route reads and writes, and any contract differences. Ask the founder about sign-in, project ownership, and Supabase deployment, then wait.
4:- [ ] Local stack and Drizzle. Run the Supabase CLI local stack. Set up the Drizzle client and configuration, the schema and first migration, and one command to migrate an empty database. Enable RLS on every table.
5:- [ ] Auth. Verify sign-in, sign-out, middleware session refresh, and first-sign-in profile creation. Require auth in `/api/chat` and every data route. Ask designers to sign in before the first send.
6:- [ ] Access helpers. Resolve and verify ownership for projects, conversations, messages, turns, events, sandboxes, and settings. Use the helpers in every data route and return one shared error for missing and unauthorized resources.
7:- [ ] Projects and conversations. Create the project, conversation, and sandbox ID on first send. Restore chat with thinking and reasoning parts intact and reconnect the sandbox after reload or on another browser. Remove the matching localStorage state.
8:- [ ] Turns, events and settings. Write turn record v2 product fields to `turns` and log restore, keep, approve, and deny with their reasons in `events`. Persist and clamp Settings on the server. Verify settings changes affect the next turn's config hash and Context & cost totals come from `turns`.
9:- [ ] Authorization test. Add a member and outsider test and a two-user script. Verify user B receives the same error on every route for every resource owned by user A, including sandbox IDs and settings.
10:- [ ] Consent. Store consent in `user_settings` and verify that an exported Langfuse trace contains only metadata when consent is off.
11:- [ ] Runner isolation. Run `agent:run` without signing in. Verify it uses defaults and writes nothing to user tables.
12:- [ ] Failure states. Verify readable errors or safe fallbacks for database downtime, expired sessions, invalid settings, and failed turn writes. Log failed writes and keep chat working.
14:## Study and plan
18:### Onlook v1
24:### Proposed schema and routes
31:| `user_settings` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema | `user_id uuid` (PK and FK to `users`), `settings jsonb` | New `GET /api/settings` reads the session user's row. New `PUT /api/settings` validates, clamps, and upserts it. `POST /api/chat` reads it for effective agent settings and trace consent. |
34:| `messages` | `id bigint` (server-assigned identity, serialized as a string for `UIMessage.id`), `conversation_id uuid` (FK to `conversations`), `role`, `parts jsonb`, `metadata jsonb`, `usage jsonb` (nullable), `created_at`. `parts`, `metadata`, and `usage` are pending turn record v2 / settings schema. | `POST /api/chat` loads stored history, appends validated user input and the server-produced assistant message, and resolves approval responses to stored requests. `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads messages in append order. |
35:| `turns` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema | `id uuid` (agent turn ID), `message_id bigint` (FK to the assistant `messages` row), `trace_id text`, `checkpoint_id text` (nullable), `status text`, `stop_reason text` (nullable), `provider text`, `model text`, `config_hash text`, `input_tokens bigint`, `output_tokens bigint`, `cache_read_tokens bigint`, `cache_write_tokens bigint`, `cost_usd numeric` (nullable), `created_at` | `POST /api/chat` writes a product summary when the agent turn settles. `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads turn data for history and aggregates that conversation's totals for Context & cost. `POST /api/restore` and `POST /api/events` resolve the owned turn. |
36:| `events` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema | `id bigint` (identity), `turn_id uuid` (FK to `turns`), `type` (`restore`, `keep`, `approve`, `deny`), `reason text`, `tool_call_id text` (nullable), `created_at` | `POST /api/restore` records a successful restore. `POST /api/events` appends keep. `POST /api/chat` records approve or deny against the turn that requested approval. `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads action state for restored history. |
38:### Contract differences and pending mappings
40:- **`user_settings.settings` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** The shared server schema supplies the JSONB type, clamps and defaults for models and effort per route, thinking display, step cap, per-turn budget and cost cap, tool toggles, protected paths, approval mode, context editing and compaction, and trace consent. Parse and clamp on both reads and writes, with safe defaults for missing or invalid rows. Use the resolved settings for each turn so a saved change is reflected in the next effective config hash. Source: current `lib/agent/config.ts` and `lib/agent/run.ts` under `apps/web/src`.
41:- **`messages.parts`, `messages.metadata`, `messages.usage` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** Persist server-produced AI SDK parts, including unchanged thinking and reasoning, with no client-supplied assistant history. The proposed extra `metadata` column carries the selected model and server-generated UI notice, which the current renderer uses. Rehydrate turn ID, trace ID and status from the linked turn. Append approval events and continuations and preserve the original message rows. Sources: `lib/agent/types.ts`, `lib/agent/client.ts`, `lib/agent/run.ts`, and `components/ai/Message.tsx` under `apps/web/src`.
42:- **`turns` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** Confirm turn and message linkage, trace and checkpoint IDs, status and stop reason, provider and model, effective config hash, each token counter, cost, and the creation timestamp. The baseline has separate system prompt and tool config hashes, `stepLimitReached` and optional error text, nested nullable `checkpoint.id`, and `startedAt` and `endedAt`. Usage has input, output and `cachedInputTokens`, plus nullable `costUsd` initialized to `null`. It collects cache reads and exposes no cache-write total or explicit stop reason. Use the final record for these mappings. Sources: `lib/agent/types.ts` and `lib/agent/run.ts` under `apps/web/src`.
43:- **`events` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** Confirm the turn link, event types, reason, tool-call correlation and timestamp. The baseline has `at`, optional `traceId`, a `checkpointId` for restore, and `toolCallId` for approve and deny. There is no event `reason`, and approvals are currently logged at continuation. The proposed `tool_call_id` preserves which request was answered when a turn has multiple tool calls. Resolve trace and checkpoint IDs from the owned turn. Sources: `lib/agent/types.ts`, `lib/agent/events.ts`, and `lib/agent/run.ts` under `apps/web/src`.
45:### Access and persistence
51:### Founder decisions
53:1. Which sign-in methods should ship? Default is GitHub OAuth plus email magic link.
54:2. Should projects use `projects.owner_id` or a membership join table? The proposed schema uses `owner_id` for single-owner projects.
55:3. Should Supabase stay local for now or should we target Supabase Cloud as well?
59:### Evidence
65:| `bun run typecheck` | Passed | Passed |
66:| `bun run test` | 71 passed, 0 failed | 71 passed, 0 failed |

content.text: Founder answers for DB-1: (1) Sign-in: GitHub OAuth plus email magic link; in local dev use the Supabase local stack's built-in mail catcher for magic links, no real email provider. (2) Projects: owner id on each project, no members table until sharing exists. (3) Supabase: local only for now; the founder creates the cloud project later and will say so. Record these in db-progress.md and tick Study and plan. Then do the next item, Local stack and Drizzle, for the tables that do not depend on AI-CORE-2 (users, projects, conversations, messages, events); keep turns and user_settings as pending until turn record v2 and the settings schema land, and say so. # AGENTS.md

Rules for every coding agent on Betterlook, Claude and Codex alike. Claude Code reads this through `CLAUDE.md`.

Read `PROBLEM.md` before any task. It decides scope, and where anything conflicts with it, it wins.

## What this is

Betterlook is a web visual editor. A designer describes a UI change in plain language, an agent edits the real code of their React app, and Betterlook checks the edit before the designer is told it worked. It is built from scratch: Onlook is the product we improve on, not a codebase we use. No Onlook code, dependencies or docs are copied in.

## Product rules

- **An MVP.** Build what `PROBLEM.md` needs and nothing else. Deletion over addition.
- **No failure, no work.** A new check, metric, judge, fixture or feature names the observed failure that drove it: a trace, or a row in `PROBLEM.md`'s failure table. Without one, it isn't built.
- **Eval order.** Read traces, then name the failure, then a deterministic check (build, diff scope, rendered UI). A judge comes only where code can't decide, and only after it agrees with human labels.
- **Humans write the eval content.** Rubrics, judge prompts, golden labels and safety fixtures are written by the team. A coding agent builds the harness that runs them, and never writes or edits their content. Where a task needs one, leave a clearly empty slot and say so in the handoff.
- **Reliability is `pass^k`.** One passing run proves nothing. Report pass^k over a frozen suite, per model.
- **Hidden machinery.** The designer sees the edit and its outcome. Evals, traces and judges add no screen, control or setting to the designer's UI.
- **Keys stay the user's.** Users bring their own model keys. Keys are never logged, traced, committed or sent anywhere but their provider. Traces redact secrets before they are written to disk.
- **No training.** Nothing fine-tunes, distils or trains on user data.
- **English only.** No translations, no changesets.

## Code rules

- **Understand, then reuse.** Trace the behaviour end to end and fix the root cause. Before writing anything, reuse what the repo already has, then the standard library, then the platform, then an installed dependency. Add a dependency only when none of those can do it, and say why in the handoff.
- **Task-only diff.** Change only what the task needs: no renames, reformatting or cleanup of nearby code.
- **Tests.** A reproducible bug gets a failing test first, then the fix. Non-trivial logic leaves one small test behind. No new test framework.
- **Verify twice.** Run the checks in two separate clean runs before handing off. Both must pass.
- **No speculative code.** No abstraction with one user, no config for a value that never changes, no scaffolding for later.
- **Comments.** None by default. One short line only when it prevents a likely mistake a better name can't.
- **Docs** state present-tense rules, and change in the same commit as the code that makes them wrong.
- **Commits:** `type(scope): what changed`, present tense. Types `feat|fix|chore|docs|test|refactor|perf|build|ci`. No AI, model or tool attribution in commits, PRs, branch names or code.
- **Nothing private in the tree:** no keys, emails, personal names or internal links.

Claude sessions apply these through the `carmy` and `ponytail` skills and run `ponytail-review` on the diff before handoff. Codex sessions apply them through `carmy`. Any React change runs `npx react-doctor@latest` and fixes what it reports. Outside research uses `agent-reach`, and any claim that drives a decision cites its source.

## Working as one of several agents

Several agents work on Betterlook at once, each in its own workspace and branch, coordinated by an orchestrator.

- One task, one branch. Change only the files your task names. If you need to touch another file, stop and report it as blocked.
- Never merge, rebase onto, or push to the base branch. The orchestrator integrates.
- Commit on your branch only when your task says to.

checks: <commands and outcomes, both runs>
handoff: <next-step context or none>

# PROBLEM.md

The problem Betterlook solves. Every change in this repository serves it. When a doc, a habit or an Onlook feature conflicts with this file, this file wins.

## Statement

**Betterlook** is a visual editor where designers describe a UI change in plain language and an AI agent edits the real code of their React app. Onlook already makes the edit. It does not know whether the edit was good. Today an edit can break the build, touch code outside the request, regress the layout, behave differently on a second run, or follow an instruction hidden in a file or web page, and the designer is the one who finds out.

**We are handling evals.** The job is to make Betterlook's agent measurably controlled and confident, without the designer seeing any of the machinery:

- Learn how the agent actually fails by reading real traces, before choosing any metric.
- Check every edit against the real outcome (build, diff scope, rendered UI) with deterministic checks first, and narrow, human-calibrated judges only where code can't decide.
- Block regressions before merge, and measure reliability across repeated runs (`pass^k`), not one lucky run.
- Trace every session with secrets redacted, so real failures become new test cases.
- Prove that prompt and harness changes improve the agent on a frozen suite, across the models users choose.

## Constraints

- No model training of any kind.
- Users bring their own model keys.
- The team writes every rubric, judge, label and safety fixture by hand.
- The frontend is a new minimal Astryx shell.
- Cut anything not driven by an observed failure.

## The failures we know of

These are the failures the statement names. A new one joins this list only from a real trace.

| Failure | What the designer sees today |
|---|---|
| Build breaks | The app stops rendering after the edit. |
| Out-of-scope diff | Files or code the request never mentioned changed. |
| Layout regression | Something other than the requested element moved or broke. |
| Nondeterminism | The same request gives a different result on a second run. |
| Prompt injection | The agent followed an instruction found in a file or web page, not the designer's. |

## Done means

- A designer's edit is checked against the build, the diff and the rendered UI before they are told it worked.
- A prompt or harness change merges only if it does no worse on the frozen suite, measured as `pass^k`, on every model users can pick.
- Every session leaves a redacted trace, and a failure found in one can become a test case.
- None of this adds a screen, a control or a wait the designer has to manage.

## Decisions

- Betterlook is a web app, built from scratch, frontend and agent backend alike. No Onlook code is reused; Onlook is only the product we measure against.
- English only. No translations, no changesets.

# DB progress

- [ ] Study and plan. Read the Betterlook turn record and settings schema, then the specified Onlook v1 files and authorization commit. Record what to keep and drop, the ownership model and access helpers, tables and columns, route reads and writes, and any contract differences. Ask the founder about sign-in, project ownership, and Supabase deployment, then wait.
- [ ] Local stack and Drizzle. Run the Supabase CLI local stack. Set up the Drizzle client and configuration, the schema and first migration, and one command to migrate an empty database. Enable RLS on every table.
- [ ] Auth. Verify sign-in, sign-out, middleware session refresh, and first-sign-in profile creation. Require auth in `/api/chat` and every data route. Ask designers to sign in before the first send.
- [ ] Access helpers. Resolve and verify ownership for projects, conversations, messages, turns, events, sandboxes, and settings. Use the helpers in every data route and return one shared error for missing and unauthorized resources.
- [ ] Projects and conversations. Create the project, conversation, and sandbox ID on first send. Restore chat with thinking and reasoning parts intact and reconnect the sandbox after reload or on another browser. Remove the matching localStorage state.
- [ ] Turns, events and settings. Write turn record v2 product fields to `turns` and log restore, keep, approve, and deny with their reasons in `events`. Persist and clamp Settings on the server. Verify settings changes affect the next turn's config hash and Context & cost totals come from `turns`.
- [ ] Authorization test. Add a member and outsider test and a two-user script. Verify user B receives the same error on every route for every resource owned by user A, including sandbox IDs and settings.
- [ ] Consent. Store consent in `user_settings` and verify that an exported Langfuse trace contains only metadata when consent is off.
- [ ] Runner isolation. Run `agent:run` without signing in. Verify it uses defaults and writes nothing to user tables.
- [ ] Failure states. Verify readable errors or safe fallbacks for database downtime, expired sessions, invalid settings, and failed turn writes. Log failed writes and keep chat working.

## Study and plan

Baseline is `betterlook` at `8ceb7805`. The agent exposes the original `TurnRecord`, `TurnEvent`, and `AgentMessage` types, and `runAgent()` returns both the UI stream and a turn promise. Agent limits and tool policy are static. No Settings schema or localStorage-backed Settings panel is present on this ref. The workspace stores chat and sandbox ID in localStorage. Sources: `apps/web/src/lib/agent/types.ts`, `config.ts`, `run.ts`, `policy.ts`, and `apps/web/src/workspace/Workspace.tsx`.

### Onlook v1

- Keep the Supabase-managed `auth.users` reference, the matching public profile with cascading delete, and the project → conversation → message hierarchy with typed JSONB message parts. Use Supabase SSR cookies and Next's session-refresh proxy, with `auth.getUser()` in server handlers. Use server-only Drizzle over postgres-js with `prepare: false` and a development-cached connection. Use the Supabase CLI local stack and drizzle-kit with Supabase roles, public-schema migrations under `supabase/migrations`, and RLS on every product table. Sources: `upstream/v1:packages/db/src/schema/`, `packages/db/src/client.ts`, `packages/db/drizzle.config.ts`, `apps/web/client/src/proxy.ts`, `apps/web/client/src/utils/supabase/`, and `apps/web/client/src/server/api/trpc.ts`.
- Drop the role join table for the single-owner MVP, pending founder confirmation. Keep the existing Next route handlers. Omit upstream tRPC, browser data and storage access, branches, canvas, frames, domains, subscriptions, invitations, and extra project and message fields. Sources: `upstream/v1:packages/db/src/schema/user/user-project.ts`, `project/project.ts`, `chat/conversation.ts`, `chat/message.ts`, and `apps/web/client/src/utils/supabase/client/index.ts`.
- Onlook's Drizzle connection bypassed RLS. A signed-in user was sufficient for routes that skipped membership checks, exposing other users' resources. The fix applied resolve-then-verify checks, scoped provider sandbox listings and pinned self-service writes to the session. Its sandbox guard still allowed IDs without a project for bootstrap. Betterlook provisions a sandbox server-side for an owned project and records the association before accepting reconnect or restore requests. A supplied sandbox ID without an owned project gets the shared resource error. Source: `git show 423e2e92`.

### Proposed schema and routes

`id` is the primary key unless stated otherwise. All timestamps use `timestamptz`. Foreign keys follow the ownership chain and cascade on deletion. `auth.users` is a reference managed by Supabase. Route names marked new are proposed.

| Table | Columns | Route reads and writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `users` | `id uuid` (PK and FK to `auth.users.id`), `created_at` | The Supabase sign-in callback verifies the user and inserts the profile idempotently. |
| `user_settings` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema | `user_id uuid` (PK and FK to `users`), `settings jsonb` | New `GET /api/settings` reads the session user's row. New `PUT /api/settings` validates, clamps, and upserts it. `POST /api/chat` reads it for effective agent settings and trace consent. |
| `projects` | `id uuid`, `owner_id uuid` (FK to `users`), `name text`, `sandbox_id text` (unique and nullable during provisioning), `created_at`, `updated_at` | `POST /api/chat` creates the project on first send and records the provisioned sandbox. New `GET /api/projects` lists the caller's projects and their conversations. `POST /api/sandbox` reconnects the project's sandbox. `POST /api/restore` uses the sandbox resolved from the turn. |
| `conversations` | `id uuid`, `project_id uuid` (FK to `projects`), `created_at`, `updated_at` | `POST /api/chat` creates the first conversation and updates its timestamp on new activity. `GET /api/projects` lists owned conversations. New `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads the owned conversation, history, and usage totals. |
| `messages` | `id bigint` (server-assigned identity, serialized as a string for `UIMessage.id`), `conversation_id uuid` (FK to `conversations`), `role`, `parts jsonb`, `metadata jsonb`, `usage jsonb` (nullable), `created_at`. `parts`, `metadata`, and `usage` are pending turn record v2 / settings schema. | `POST /api/chat` loads stored history, appends validated user input and the server-produced assistant message, and resolves approval responses to stored requests. `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads messages in append order. |
| `turns` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema | `id uuid` (agent turn ID), `message_id bigint` (FK to the assistant `messages` row), `trace_id text`, `checkpoint_id text` (nullable), `status text`, `stop_reason text` (nullable), `provider text`, `model text`, `config_hash text`, `input_tokens bigint`, `output_tokens bigint`, `cache_read_tokens bigint`, `cache_write_tokens bigint`, `cost_usd numeric` (nullable), `created_at` | `POST /api/chat` writes a product summary when the agent turn settles. `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads turn data for history and aggregates that conversation's totals for Context & cost. `POST /api/restore` and `POST /api/events` resolve the owned turn. |
| `events` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema | `id bigint` (identity), `turn_id uuid` (FK to `turns`), `type` (`restore`, `keep`, `approve`, `deny`), `reason text`, `tool_call_id text` (nullable), `created_at` | `POST /api/restore` records a successful restore. `POST /api/events` appends keep. `POST /api/chat` records approve or deny against the turn that requested approval. `GET /api/conversations/[id]` reads action state for restored history. |

### Contract differences and pending mappings

- **`user_settings.settings` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** The shared server schema supplies the JSONB type, clamps and defaults for models and effort per route, thinking display, step cap, per-turn budget and cost cap, tool toggles, protected paths, approval mode, context editing and compaction, and trace consent. Parse and clamp on both reads and writes, with safe defaults for missing or invalid rows. Use the resolved settings for each turn so a saved change is reflected in the next effective config hash. Source: current `lib/agent/config.ts` and `lib/agent/run.ts` under `apps/web/src`.
- **`messages.parts`, `messages.metadata`, `messages.usage` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** Persist server-produced AI SDK parts, including unchanged thinking and reasoning, with no client-supplied assistant history. The proposed extra `metadata` column carries the selected model and server-generated UI notice, which the current renderer uses. Rehydrate turn ID, trace ID and status from the linked turn. Append approval events and continuations and preserve the original message rows. Sources: `lib/agent/types.ts`, `lib/agent/client.ts`, `lib/agent/run.ts`, and `components/ai/Message.tsx` under `apps/web/src`.
- **`turns` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** Confirm turn and message linkage, trace and checkpoint IDs, status and stop reason, provider and model, effective config hash, each token counter, cost, and the creation timestamp. The baseline has separate system prompt and tool config hashes, `stepLimitReached` and optional error text, nested nullable `checkpoint.id`, and `startedAt` and `endedAt`. Usage has input, output and `cachedInputTokens`, plus nullable `costUsd` initialized to `null`. It collects cache reads and exposes no cache-write total or explicit stop reason. Use the final record for these mappings. Sources: `lib/agent/types.ts` and `lib/agent/run.ts` under `apps/web/src`.
- **`events` — pending turn record v2 / settings schema.** Confirm the turn link, event types, reason, tool-call correlation and timestamp. The baseline has `at`, optional `traceId`, a `checkpointId` for restore, and `toolCallId` for approve and deny. There is no event `reason`, and approvals are currently logged at continuation. The proposed `tool_call_id` preserves which request was answered when a turn has multiple tool calls. Resolve trace and checkpoint IDs from the owned turn. Sources: `lib/agent/types.ts`, `lib/agent/events.ts`, and `lib/agent/run.ts` under `apps/web/src`.

### Access and persistence

- `requireUser` verifies the Supabase user for data routes. `requireProject` scopes by `projects.owner_id`. `requireConversation`, `requireMessage`, `requireTurn`, and `requireEvent` follow the stored parent chain to that project. `requireSandbox` maps the sandbox ID to that same owned project. `requireSettings` scopes by the authenticated user ID. Project lists and settings writes derive the owner from the session. Signed-in requests for missing or foreign resources get the same `404` and `Unauthorized or not found` body. A request with multiple IDs must resolve them to the same resource chain before any tool, provider, checkpoint, trace or write operation. Enable RLS on each product table as defense in depth and keep the browser on Supabase Auth only.
- `/api/chat` currently takes browser-supplied history and sandbox ID. Use the owned conversation's saved history and project sandbox, validate the submitted user input or approval, and verify an approval against its stored pending tool call. `/api/restore` derives checkpoint, sandbox and trace IDs from the owned turn. `/api/events` derives the trace ID the same way. # AGENTS.md

Rules for every coding agent on Betterlook, Claude and Codex alike. Claude Code reads this through `CLAUDE.md`.

Read `PROBLEM.md` before any task. It decides scope, and where anything conflicts with it, it wins.

## What this is

Betterlook is a web visual editor. A designer describes a UI change in plain language, an agent edits the real code of their React app, and Betterlook checks the edit before the designer is told it worked. It is built from scratch: Onlook is the product we improve on, not a codebase we use. No Onlook code, dependencies or docs are copied in.

## Product rules

- **An MVP.** Build what `PROBLEM.md` needs and nothing else. Deletion over addition.
- **No failure, no work.** A new check, metric, judge, fixture or feature names the observed failure that drove it: a trace, or a row in `PROBLEM.md`'s failure table. Without one, it isn't built.
- **Eval order.** Read traces, then name the failure, then a deterministic check (build, diff scope, rendered UI). A judge comes only where code can't decide, and only after it agrees with human labels.
- **Humans write the eval content.** Rubrics, judge prompts, golden labels and safety fixtures are written by the team. A coding agent builds the harness that runs them, and never writes or edits their content. Where a task needs one, leave a clearly empty slot and say so in the handoff.
- **Reliability is `pass^k`.** One passing run proves nothing. Report pass^k over a frozen suite, per model.
- **Hidden machinery.** The designer sees the edit and its outcome. Evals, traces and judges add no screen, control or setting to the designer's UI.
- **Keys stay the user's.** Users bring their own model keys. Keys are never logged, traced, committed or sent anywhere but their provider. Traces redact secrets before they are written to disk.
- **No training.** Nothing fine-tunes, distils or trains on user data.
- **English only.** No translations, no changesets.

## Code rules

- **Understand, then reuse.** Trace the behaviour end to end and fix the root cause. Before writing anything, reuse what the repo already has, then the standard library, then the platform, then an installed dependency. Add a dependency only when none of those can do it, and say why in the handoff.
- **Task-only diff.** Change only what the task needs: no renames, reformatting or cleanup of nearby code.
- **Tests.** A reproducible bug gets a failing test first, then the fix. Non-trivial logic leaves one small test behind. No new test framework.
- **Verify twice.** Run the checks in two separate clean runs before handing off. Both must pass.
- **No speculative code.** No abstraction with one user, no config for a value that never changes, no scaffolding for later.
- **Comments.** None by default. One short line only when it prevents a likely mistake a better name can't.
- **Docs** state present-tense rules, and change in the same commit as the code that makes them wrong.
- **Commits:** `type(scope): what changed`, present tense. Types `feat|fix|chore|docs|test|refactor|perf|build|ci`. No AI, model or tool attribution in commits, PRs, branch names or code.
- **Nothing private in the tree:** no keys, emails, personal names or internal links.

Claude sessions apply these through the `carmy` and `ponytail` skills and run `ponytail-review` on the diff before handoff. Codex sessions apply them through `carmy`. Any React change runs `npx react-doctor@latest` and fixes what it reports. Outside research uses `agent-reach`, and any claim that drives a decision cites its source.

## Working as one of several agents

Several agents work on Betterlook at once, each in its own workspace and branch, coordinated by an orchestrator.

- One task, one branch. Change only the files your task names. If you need to touch another file, stop and report it as blocked.
- Never merge, rebase onto, or push to the base branch. The orchestrator integrates.
- Commit on your branch only when your task says to.
- End your final message with exactly one of these envelopes:

```text
SUPERSET_WORKER_DONE
task: <task-id>
summary: <one-line outcome>
files: <comma-separated paths or none>
checks: <commands and outcomes, both runs>
handoff: <next-step context or none>
```

```text
SUPERSET_WORKER_BLOCKED
task: <task-id>
reason: <specific blocker>
needs: <decision, access, or dependency required>
```
# PROBLEM.md

The problem Betterlook solves. Every change in this repository serves it. When a doc, a habit or an Onlook feature conflicts with this file, this file wins.

## Statement

**Betterlook** is a visual editor where designers describe a UI change in plain language and an AI agent edits the real code of their React app. Onlook already makes the edit. It does not know whether the edit was good. Today an edit can break the build, touch code outside the request, regress the layout, behave differently on a second run, or follow an instruction hidden in a file or web page, and the designer is the one who finds out.

**We are handling evals.** The job is to make Betterlook's agent measurably controlled and confident, without the designer seeing any of the machinery:

- Learn how the agent actually fails by reading real traces, before choosing any metric.
- Check every edit against the real outcome (build, diff scope, rendered UI) with deterministic checks first, and narrow, human-calibrated judges only where code can't decide.
- Block regressions before merge, and measure reliability across repeated runs (`pass^k`), not one lucky run.
- Trace every session with secrets redacted, so real failures become new test cases.
- Prove that prompt and harness changes improve the agent on a frozen suite, across the models users choose.

## Constraints

- No model training of any kind.
- Users bring their own model keys.
- The team writes every rubric, judge, label and safety fixture by hand.
- The frontend is a new minimal Astryx shell.
- Cut anything not driven by an observed failure.

## The failures we know of

These are the failures the statement names. A new one joins this list only from a real trace.

| Failure | What the designer sees today |
|---|---|
| Build breaks | The app stops rendering after the edit. |
| Out-of-scope diff | Files or code the request never mentioned changed. |
| Layout regression | Something other than the requested element moved or broke. |
| Nondeterminism | The same request gives a different result on a second run. |
| Prompt injection | The agent followed an instruction found in a file or web page, not the designer's. |

## Done means

- A designer's edit is checked against the build, the diff and the rendered UI before they are told it worked.
- A prompt or harness change merges only if it does no worse on the frozen suite, measured as `pass^k`, on every model users can pick.
- Every session leaves a redacted trace, and a failure found in one can become a test case.
- None of this adds a screen, a control or a wait the designer has to manage.

## Decisions

- Betterlook is a web app, built from scratch, frontend and agent backend alike. No Onlook code is reused; Onlook is only the product we measure against.
- English only. No translations, no changesets.

# 网页阅读

通用网页、RSS。

## 通用网页 (Jina Reader)

```bash
# 读取任意网页内容
curl -s "https://r.jina.ai/URL"

# 示例
curl -s "https://r.jina.ai/https://example.com/article"
```

**适用场景**: 大多数网页可以直接用 Jina Reader 读取。

## Web Reader (MCP)

```bash
# 读取网页内容 (Markdown 格式)
mcporter call web-reader.webReader url="https://example.com"

# 保留图片
mcporter call web-reader.webReader url="https://example.com" retain_images=true

# 纯文本格式
mcporter call web-reader.webReader url="https://example.com" return_format="text"
```

**适用场景**: 需要更精确控制输出格式时使用。

## RSS (feedparser)

```python
python3 -c "
import feedparser
for e in feedparser.parse('FEED_URL').entries[:5]:
    print(f'{e.title} — {e.link}')
"
```

**适用场景**: 订阅博客、新闻源、播客等 RSS feed。

| 场景 | 推荐工具 |
|-----|---------|
| 通用网页 | Jina Reader (`curl r.jina.ai`) |
| 需要图片/格式控制 | web-reader MCP |
| RSS 订阅 | feedparser |

+ALTER TABLE "projects" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE "users" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

# AGENTS.md

Rules for every coding agent on Betterlook, Claude and Codex alike. Claude Code reads this through `CLAUDE.md`.

Read `PROBLEM.md` before any task. It decides scope, and where anything conflicts with it, it wins.

## What this is

Betterlook is a web visual editor. A designer describes a UI change in plain language, an agent edits the real code of their React app, and Betterlook checks the edit before the designer is told it worked. It is built from scratch: Onlook is the product we improve on, not a codebase we use. No Onlook code, dependencies or docs are copied in.

## Product rules

- **An MVP.** Build what `PROBLEM.md` needs and nothing else. Deletion over addition.
- **No failure, no work.** A new check, metric, judge, fixture or feature names the observed failure that drove it: a trace, or a row in `PROBLEM.md`'s failure table. Without one, it isn't built.
- **Eval order.** Read traces, then name the failure, then a deterministic check (build, diff scope, rendered UI). A judge comes only where code can't decide, and only after it agrees with human labels.
- **Humans write the eval content.** Rubrics, judge prompts, golden labels and safety fixtures are written by the team. A coding agent builds the harness that runs them, and never writes or edits their content. Where a task needs one, leave a clearly empty slot and say so in the handoff.
- **Reliability is `pass^k`.** One passing run proves nothing. Report pass^k over a frozen suite, per model.
- **Hidden machinery.** The designer sees the edit and its outcome. Evals, traces and judges add no screen, control or setting to the designer's UI.
- **Keys stay the user's.** Users bring their own model keys. Keys are never logged, traced, committed or sent anywhere but their provider. Traces redact secrets before they are written to disk.
- **No training.** Nothing fine-tunes, distils or trains on user data.
- **English only.** No translations, no changesets.

## Code rules

- **Understand, then reuse.** Trace the behaviour end to end and fix the root cause. Before writing anything, reuse what the repo already has, then the standard library, then the platform, then an installed dependency. Add a dependency only when none of those can do it, and say why in the handoff.
- **Task-only diff.** Change only what the task needs: no renames, reformatting or cleanup of nearby code.
- **Tests.** A reproducible bug gets a failing test first, then the fix. Non-trivial logic leaves one small test behind. No new test framework.
- **Verify twice.** Run the checks in two separate clean runs before handing off. Both must pass.
- **No speculative code.** No abstraction with one user, no config for a value that never changes, no scaffolding for later.
- **Comments.** None by default. One short line only when it prevents a likely mistake a better name can't.
- **Docs** state present-tense rules, and change in the same commit as the code that makes them wrong.
- **Commits:** `type(scope): what changed`, present tense. Types `feat|fix|chore|docs|test|refactor|perf|build|ci`. No AI, model or tool attribution in commits, PRs, branch names or code.
- **Nothing private in the tree:** no keys, emails, personal names or internal links.

Claude sessions apply these through the `carmy` and `ponytail` skills and run `ponytail-review` on the diff before handoff. Codex sessions apply them through `carmy`. Any React change runs `npx react-doctor@latest` and fixes what it reports. Outside research uses `agent-reach`, and any claim that drives a decision cites its source.

## Working as one of several agents

Several agents work on Betterlook at once, each in its own workspace and branch, coordinated by an orchestrator.

- One task, one branch. Change only the files your task names. If you need to touch another file, stop and report it as blocked.
- Never merge, rebase onto, or push to the base branch. The orchestrator integrates.
- Commit on your branch only when your task says to.
- End your final message with exactly one of these envelopes:

```text
SUPERSET_WORKER_DONE
task: <task-id>
summary: <one-line outcome>
files: <comma-separated paths or none>
checks: <commands and outcomes, both runs>
handoff: <next-step context or none>
```

```text
SUPERSET_WORKER_BLOCKED
task: <task-id>
reason: <specific blocker>
needs: <decision, access, or dependency required>
```
# PROBLEM.md

The problem Betterlook solves. Every change in this repository serves it. When a doc, a habit or an Onlook feature conflicts with this file, this file wins.

## Statement

**Betterlook** is a visual editor where designers describe a UI change in plain language and an AI agent edits the real code of their React app. Onlook already makes the edit. It does not know whether the edit was good. Today an edit can break the build, touch code outside the request, regress the layout, behave differently on a second run, or follow an instruction hidden in a file or web page, and the designer is the one who finds out.

**We are handling evals.** The job is to make Betterlook's agent measurably controlled and confident, without the designer seeing any of the machinery:

- Learn how the agent actually fails by reading real traces, before choosing any metric.
- Check every edit against the real outcome (build, diff scope, rendered UI) with deterministic checks first, and narrow, human-calibrated judges only where code can't decide.
- Block regressions before merge, and measure reliability across repeated runs (`pass^k`), not one lucky run.
- Trace every session with secrets redacted, so real failures become new test cases.
- Prove that prompt and harness changes improve the agent on a frozen suite, across the models users choose.

## Constraints

- No model training of any kind.
- Users bring their own model keys.
- The team writes every rubric, judge, label and safety fixture by hand.
- The frontend is a new minimal Astryx shell.
- Cut anything not driven by an observed failure.

## The failures we know of

These are the failures the statement names. A new one joins this list only from a real trace.

| Failure | What the designer sees today |
|---|---|
| Build breaks | The app stops rendering after the edit. |
| Out-of-scope diff | Files or code the request never mentioned changed. |
| Layout regression | Something other than the requested element moved or broke. |
| Nondeterminism | The same request gives a different result on a second run. |
| Prompt injection | The agent followed an instruction found in a file or web page, not the designer's. |

## Done means

- A designer's edit is checked against the build, the diff and the rendered UI before they are told it worked.
- A prompt or harness change merges only if it does no worse on the frozen suite, measured as `pass^k`, on every model users can pick.
- Every session leaves a redacted trace, and a failure found in one can become a test case.
- None of this adds a screen, a control or a wait the designer has to manage.

## Decisions

- Betterlook is a web app, built from scratch, frontend and agent backend alike. No Onlook code is reused; Onlook is only the product we measure against.
- English only. No translations, no changesets.

set -euo pipefail
for db_review_run in 1 2; do
  (
    set -euo pipefail
    db_review_dir=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/betterlook-db-final.XXXXXXXX")
    git archive HEAD | tar -xf - -C "$db_review_dir"
    tar -cf - package.json bun.lock apps/web/package.json apps/web/drizzle.config.ts apps/web/src/lib/db apps/web/src/lib/supabase supabase/migrations | tar -xf - -C "$db_review_dir"
    cd "$db_review_dir"
    printf 'Clean verification %s\n' "$db_review_run"
    env -i PATH="$PATH" BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/.bun/install/cache" bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
    (cd apps/web && env -i PATH="$PATH" NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 node ./node_modules/next/dist/bin/next typegen)
    env -i PATH="$PATH" bun run typecheck
    if ! env -i PATH="$PATH" bun run test > test-output.log 2>&1; then cat test-output.log; exit 1; fi
    tail -n 5 test-output.log
    (
      cd apps/web
      before_sql=$(shasum -a 256 ../../supabase/migrations/0000_product_tables.sql)
      env -i PATH="$PATH" node ./node_modules/drizzle-kit/bin.cjs check
      env -i PATH="$PATH" node ./node_modules/drizzle-kit/bin.cjs generate --name=product_tables
      test "$before_sql" = "$(shasum -a 256 ../../supabase/migrations/0000_product_tables.sql)"
      test "$(find ../../supabase/migrations -maxdepth 1 -name '*.sql' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = 1
      env -i PATH="$PATH" NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bun run build
      mkdir src/app/secret-boundary-probe
      cat > src/app/secret-boundary-probe/page.tsx <<'EOF'
'use client';
import {getSupabaseSecretKey} from '@/lib/supabase/server-env';

export default function SecretBoundaryProbe() {
  return <button onClick={() => { getSupabaseSecretKey(); }}>Test</button>;
}
EOF
      if env -i PATH="$PATH" NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bun run build > boundary-output.log 2>&1; then
        printf 'Client import unexpectedly built\n'
        exit 1
      fi
      if ! rg -m 4 -e "You're importing a component that needs .server-only." -e "Server-only module" -e "cannot be imported from a Client Component" boundary-output.log; then
        cat boundary-output.log
        exit 1
      fi
    )
  )
done

# AGENTS.md

Rules for every coding agent on Betterlook, Claude and Codex alike. Claude Code reads this through `CLAUDE.md`.

Read `PROBLEM.md` before any task. It decides scope, and where anything conflicts with it, it wins.

## What this is

Betterlook is a web visual editor. A designer describes a UI change in plain language, an agent edits the real code of their React app, and Betterlook checks the edit before the designer is told it worked. It is built from scratch: Onlook is the product we improve on, not a codebase we use. No Onlook code, dependencies or docs are copied in.

## Product rules

- **An MVP.** Build what `PROBLEM.md` needs and nothing else. Deletion over addition.
- **No failure, no work.** A new check, metric, judge, fixture or feature names the observed failure that drove it: a trace, or a row in `PROBLEM.md`'s failure table. Without one, it isn't built.
- **Eval order.** Read traces, then name the failure, then a deterministic check (build, diff scope, rendered UI). A judge comes only where code can't decide, and only after it agrees with human labels.
- **Humans write the eval content.** Rubrics, judge prompts, golden labels and safety fixtures are written by the team. A coding agent builds the harness that runs them, and never writes or edits their content. Where a task needs one, leave a clearly empty slot and say so in the handoff.
- **Reliability is `pass^k`.** One passing run proves nothing. Report pass^k over a frozen suite, per model.
- **Hidden machinery.** The designer sees the edit and its outcome. Evals, traces and judges add no screen, control or setting to the designer's UI.
- **Keys stay the user's.** Users bring their own model keys. Keys are never logged, traced, committed or sent anywhere but their provider. Traces redact secrets before they are written to disk.
- **No training.** Nothing fine-tunes, distils or trains on user data.
- **English only.** No translations, no changesets.

## Code rules

- **Understand, then reuse.** Trace the behaviour end to end and fix the root cause. Before writing anything, reuse what the repo already has, then the standard library, then the platform, then an installed dependency. Add a dependency only when none of those can do it, and say why in the handoff.
- **Task-only diff.** Change only what the task needs: no renames, reformatting or cleanup of nearby code.
- **Tests.** A reproducible bug gets a failing test first, then the fix. Non-trivial logic leaves one small test behind. No new test framework.
- **Verify twice.** Run the checks in two separate clean runs before handing off. Both must pass.
- **No speculative code.** No abstraction with one user, no config for a value that never changes, no scaffolding for later.
- **Comments.** None by default. One short line only when it prevents a likely mistake a better name can't.
- **Docs** state present-tense rules, and change in the same commit as the code that makes them wrong.
- **Commits:** `type(scope): what changed`, present tense. Types `feat|fix|chore|docs|test|refactor|perf|build|ci`. No AI, model or tool attribution in commits, PRs, branch names or code.
- **Nothing private in the tree:** no keys, emails, personal names or internal links.

Claude sessions apply these through the `carmy` and `ponytail` skills and run `ponytail-review` on the diff before handoff. Codex sessions apply them through `carmy`. Any React change runs `npx react-doctor@latest` and fixes what it reports. Outside research uses `agent-reach`, and any claim that drives a decision cites its source.

## Working as one of several agents

Several agents work on Betterlook at once, each in its own workspace and branch, coordinated by an orchestrator.

- One task, one branch. Change only the files your task names. If you need to touch another file, stop and report it as blocked.
- Never merge, rebase onto, or push to the base branch. The orchestrator integrates.
- Commit on your branch only when your task says to.
- End your final message with exactly one of these envelopes:

```text
SUPERSET_WORKER_DONE
task: <task-id>
summary: <one-line outcome>
files: <comma-separated paths or none>
checks: <commands and outcomes, both runs>
handoff: <next-step context or none>
```

```text
SUPERSET_WORKER_BLOCKED
task: <task-id>
reason: <specific blocker>
needs: <decision, access, or dependency required>
```
# PROBLEM.md

The problem Betterlook solves. Every change in this repository serves it. When a doc, a habit or an Onlook feature conflicts with this file, this file wins.

## Statement

**Betterlook** is a visual editor where designers describe a UI change in plain language and an AI agent edits the real code of their React app. Onlook already makes the edit. It does not know whether the edit was good. Today an edit can break the build, touch code outside the request, regress the layout, behave differently on a second run, or follow an instruction hidden in a file or web page, and the designer is the one who finds out.

**We are handling evals.** The job is to make Betterlook's agent measurably controlled and confident, without the designer seeing any of the machinery:

- Learn how the agent actually fails by reading real traces, before choosing any metric.
- Check every edit against the real outcome (build, diff scope, rendered UI) with deterministic checks first, and narrow, human-calibrated judges only where code can't decide.

set -euo pipefail
for db_review_run in 1 2; do
  (
    set -euo pipefail
    db_review_dir=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/betterlook-db-ca.XXXXXXXX")
    git archive HEAD | tar -xf - -C "$db_review_dir"
    tar -cf - package.json bun.lock apps/web/package.json apps/web/drizzle.config.ts apps/web/next.config.mjs apps/web/src/lib/db apps/web/src/lib/supabase apps/web/supabase-ca.crt supabase/migrations | tar -xf - -C "$db_review_dir"
    cd "$db_review_dir"
    printf 'Clean verification %s\n' "$db_review_run"
    env -i PATH="$PATH" BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/.bun/install/cache" bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
    (cd apps/web && env -i PATH="$PATH" NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 node ./node_modules/next/dist/bin/next typegen)
    env -i PATH="$PATH" bun run typecheck
    if ! env -i PATH="$PATH" bun run test > test-output.log 2>&1; then cat test-output.log; exit 1; fi
    tail -n 5 test-output.log
    (
      cd apps/web
      before_sql=$(shasum -a 256 ../../supabase/migrations/0000_product_tables.sql)
      env -i PATH="$PATH" node ./node_modules/drizzle-kit/bin.cjs check
      env -i PATH="$PATH" node ./node_modules/drizzle-kit/bin.cjs generate --name=product_tables
      test "$before_sql" = "$(shasum -a 256 ../../supabase/migrations/0000_product_tables.sql)"
      test "$(find ../../supabase/migrations -maxdepth 1 -name '*.sql' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = 1
      env -i PATH="$PATH" NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bun run build
      node --input-type=module - <<'JS'

JS
      mkdir src/app/secret-boundary-probe

}
EOF
      if env -i PATH="$PATH" NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bun run build > boundary-output.log 2>&1; then

      fi
    )
  )
done

# AGENTS.md

Rules for every coding agent on Betterlook, Claude and Codex alike. Claude Code reads this through `CLAUDE.md`.

Read `PROBLEM.md` before any task. It decides scope, and where anything conflicts with it, it wins.

## What this is

Betterlook is a web visual editor. A designer describes a UI change in plain language, an agent edits the real code of their React app, and Betterlook checks the edit before the designer is told it worked. It is built from scratch: Onlook is the product we improve on, not a codebase we use. No Onlook code, dependencies or docs are copied in.

## Product rules

- **An MVP.** Build what `PROBLEM.md` needs and nothing else. Deletion over addition.
- **No failure, no work.** A new check, metric, judge, fixture or feature names the observed failure that drove it: a trace, or a row in `PROBLEM.md`'s failure table. Without one, it isn't built.
- **Eval order.** Read traces, then name the failure, then a deterministic check (build, diff scope, rendered UI). A judge comes only where code can't decide, and only after it agrees with human labels.
- **Humans write the eval content.** Rubrics, judge prompts, golden labels and safety fixtures are written by the team. A coding agent builds the harness that runs them, and never writes or edits their content. Where a task needs one, leave a clearly empty slot and say so in the handoff.
- **Reliability is `pass^k`.** One passing run proves nothing. Report pass^k over a frozen suite, per model.
- **Hidden machinery.** The designer sees the edit and its outcome. Evals, traces and judges add no screen, control or setting to the designer's UI.
- **Keys stay the user's.** Users bring their own model keys. Keys are never logged, traced, committed or sent anywhere but their provider. Traces redact secrets before they are written to disk.
- **No training.** Nothing fine-tunes, distils or trains on user data.
- **English only.** No translations, no changesets.

## Code rules

- **Understand, then reuse.** Trace the behaviour end to end and fix the root cause. Before writing anything, reuse what the repo already has, then the standard library, then the platform, then an installed dependency. Add a dependency only when none of those can do it, and say why in the handoff.
- **Task-only diff.** Change only what the task needs: no renames, reformatting or cleanup of nearby code.
- **Tests.** A reproducible bug gets a failing test first, then the fix. Non-trivial logic leaves one small test behind. No new test framework.
- **Verify twice.** Run the checks in two separate clean runs before handing off. Both must pass.
- **No speculative code.** No abstraction with one user, no config for a value that never changes, no scaffolding for later.
- **Comments.** None by default. One short line only when it prevents a likely mistake a better name can't.
- **Docs** state present-tense rules, and change in the same commit as the code that makes them wrong.
- **Commits:** `type(scope): what changed`, present tense. Types `feat|fix|chore|docs|test|refactor|perf|build|ci`. No AI, model or tool attribution in commits, PRs, branch names or code.
- **Nothing private in the tree:** no keys, emails, personal names or internal links.

Claude sessions apply these through the `carmy` and `ponytail` skills and run `ponytail-review` on the diff before handoff. Codex sessions apply them through `carmy`. Any React change runs `npx react-doctor@latest` and fixes what it reports. Outside research uses `agent-reach`, and any claim that drives a decision cites its source.

## Working as one of several agents

Several agents work on Betterlook at once, each in its own workspace and branch, coordinated by an orchestrator.

- One task, one branch. Change only the files your task names. If you need to touch another file, stop and report it as blocked.
- Never merge, rebase onto, or push to the base branch. The orchestrator integrates.
- Commit on your branch only when your task says to.
- End your final message with exactly one of these envelopes:

```text
SUPERSET_WORKER_DONE
task: <task-id>
summary: <one-line outcome>
files: <comma-separated paths or none>
checks: <commands and outcomes, both runs>
handoff: <next-step context or none>
```

```text
SUPERSET_WORKER_BLOCKED
task: <task-id>
reason: <specific blocker>
needs: <decision, access, or dependency required>
```
# PROBLEM.md

The problem Betterlook solves. Every change in this repository serves it. When a doc, a habit or an Onlook feature conflicts with this file, this file wins.

## Statement

**Betterlook** is a visual editor where designers describe a UI change in plain language and an AI agent edits the real code of their React app. Onlook already makes the edit. It does not know whether the edit was good. Today an edit can break the build, touch code outside the request, regress the layout, behave differently on a second run, or follow an instruction hidden in a file or web page, and the designer is the one who finds out.

**We are handling evals.** The job is to make Betterlook's agent measurably controlled and confident, without the designer seeing any of the machinery:

- Learn how the agent actually fails by reading real traces, before choosing any metric.
- Check every edit against the real outcome (build, diff scope, rendered UI) with deterministic checks first, and narrow, human-calibrated judges only where code can't decide.
- Block regressions before merge, and measure reliability across repeated runs (`pass^k`), not one lucky run.
- Trace every session with secrets redacted, so real failures become new test cases.
- Prove that prompt and harness changes improve the agent on a frozen suite, across the models users choose.

## Constraints

- No model training of any kind.
- Users bring their own model keys.
- The team writes every rubric, judge, label and safety fixture by hand.
- The frontend is a new minimal Astryx shell.
- Cut anything not driven by an observed failure.

## The failures we know of

These are the failures the statement names. A new one joins this list only from a real trace.

| Failure | What the designer sees today |
|---|---|
| Build breaks | The app stops rendering after the edit. |
| Out-of-scope diff | Files or code the request never mentioned changed. |
| Layout regression | Something other than the requested element moved or broke. |
| Nondeterminism | The same request gives a different result on a second run. |
| Prompt injection | The agent followed an instruction found in a file or web page, not the designer's. |

## Done means

- A designer's edit is checked against the build, the diff and the rendered UI before they are told it worked.
- A prompt or harness change merges only if it does no worse on the frozen suite, measured as `pass^k`, on every model users can pick.
- Every session leaves a redacted trace, and a failure found in one can become a test case.
- None of this adds a screen, a control or a wait the designer has to manage.

## Decisions

- Betterlook is a web app, built from scratch, frontend and agent backend alike. No Onlook code is reused; Onlook is only the product we measure against.
- English only. No translations, no changesets.

- No model training of any kind.
- Users bring their own model keys.
- The team writes every rubric, judge, label and safety fixture by hand.
- The frontend is a new minimal Astryx shell.
- Cut anything not driven by an observed failure.

## The failures we know of

These are the failures the statement names. A new one joins this list only from a real trace.

| Failure | What the designer sees today |
|---|---|
| Build breaks | The app stops rendering after the edit. |
| Out-of-scope diff | Files or code the request never mentioned changed. |
| Layout regression | Something other than the requested element moved or broke. |
| Nondeterminism | The same request gives a different result on a second run. |
| Prompt injection | The agent followed an instruction found in a file or web page, not the designer's. |

## Done means

- A designer's edit is checked against the build, the diff and the rendered UI before they are told it worked.
- A prompt or harness change merges only if it does no worse on the frozen suite, measured as `pass^k`, on every model users can pick.
- Every session leaves a redacted trace, and a failure found in one can become a test case.
- None of this adds a screen, a control or a wait the designer has to manage.

## Decisions

- Betterlook is a web app, built from scratch, frontend and agent backend alike. No Onlook code is reused; Onlook is only the product we measure against.
- English only. No translations, no changesets.

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

- `gpt-6.2-astra`: Our most capable model for complex coding and professional work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
